findings.reason: the plan owns its own driving chain, so with no followup naming §5 the section is not dispatchable from the plan's record and the chain closes at §5 with no invocation, which is exactly the state the plan-state contract forbids.

findings.reason: the queue orders only what the plan declares, so a dispatch admitted now launches §5 ahead of the §4 code it is written against, and the node either duplicates §4's session walk or measures a check that does not exist.
findings.text: s5's `data-links=""` declares no `plan-section-depends-on`, yet its deliverable says the refusing check is "the same live-session check §4 adds to `resume_plan`", and §4 is still `implementable`

findings.reason: an undeclared write path means the node's exclusive scope is unknowable at dispatch, so its gate measures an editable surface nobody bounded and a coordinator cannot tell an in-scope edit from a stray one.
findings.text: the write paths are "the module the reproduction names and `tests/test_a_queued_run_launches_once.py`", and the first is not a path a coordinator can fence, audit or scope a gate to until the node has already run

findings.reason: the second deliverable has no measure in the done-when at all, so it can be neither reviewed nor closed, and bundling it means the section's single gate proves neither job.
findings.text: §5 carries two unrelated deliverables: "records why attempt 1's worktree was read-only" and "that path refuses to launch a worker for a run whose recorded worker pid is alive"; the read-only question is a worktree-fence/mount defect, not a launch-constraint one

findings.reason: a worker implementing to the done-when can pass while never calling the §4 session walk, so a worker implementing to the done-when can pass while never taking the session walk §4 adds, and the section would then be reviewed as landed while the guard it exists for was never reached.
findings.text: the deliverable specifies the session check §4 adds to `resume_plan`, while the done-when measures only "a launch of a run whose first worker is alive is refused naming that pid" — the existing `record_process_alive` pid read, which is not the check §4 adds

findings.reason: the node would spend its investigation re-deriving a settled fact that is unrelated to launching twice, when it should carry that as a cited input; if the mount behaviour is itself to be repaired, it needs its own section, not this one's deliverable.
